envelope.description: Build the functional-requirements renderer as a third webview source string

body.title: Build the functional-requirements renderer as a third webview source string
body.summary: Add `DOCS_FR_SOURCE` beside DOCS_BODY_RENDERER_SOURCE and DOCS_SECTIONS_SOURCE, containing `renderFunctionalRequirements` — the first implementation of sc2's published `StructuredRenderer<FunctionalDefinition>`, returning `{ el }`. It constructs one discrete element per requirement, writes EVERY string with textContent and assigns no markup anywhere, carries id / statement / rationale, and preserves the record's doc-level-then-per-item-grouped-by-itemRef order rather than flattening it. Written in the same ES5-compatible style as its two siblings so it evaluates both inline in the webview and under `new Function` in tests. The record is treated as structurally untrusted: `requirements` not an array yields an empty container, a malformed entry is skipped while its well-formed siblings render, duplicates are preserved and an orphan `itemRef` falls into the same bucket the prose renderer uses. Also add the item CSS as one more fragment in the existing `mdStyle` concatenation, using `--it-*` variables only. Inert after this task — the string is defined and inlined but nothing calls it.
acceptanceChecks: An id containing `*`, `_`, backtick and `[` comes out of the DOM stub byte-identical to the record's value — the central falsifiable claim of this Story.
A statement containing `<script>alert(1)</script>` renders as text and creates no child element.
The renderer produces exactly one discrete element per requirement, asserted as a count against the record length and as distinct sibling nodes — not as a substring of the rendered text.
Doc-level requirements render before per-item ones, per-item requirements are grouped under their `itemRef`, and a group with no members produces no header.

ADDED (s3/t2a): a record with TWO entries sharing one FrId renders BOTH as distinct items in record order — neither dropped nor merged; a de-duplicating implementation must fail this check, because collapsing a duplicate would hide a real producer-side defect from the reviewer at the approval gate.

ADDED (s3/t2b): a `scope:'item'` entry whose `itemRef` is missing or empty is grouped under the SAME literal key the existing prose renderer uses (functional-definition.ts:99), asserted against that key rather than an invented one, so the two renderings of one record cannot disagree about where an orphan belongs.
A malformed record — `requirements` not an array, an entry that is not an object, an entry with a non-string id or statement — produces fewer items or an empty container and never throws.

The emitted shell still contains EXACTLY ONE `.innerHTML=` and it is still `el.innerHTML=marked.parse`; `DOCS_FR_SOURCE` itself contains no markup assignment, asserted with comments stripped before scanning.
Every item CSS rule references only `--it-*` variables — no `--sans`/`--fg-strong`/`--border`, which are undefined on this surface and would silently invalidate the declarations containing them.

CLOSING CONDITION (s3/t7): this task's own mutations are run here, not deferred — replacing textContent with a concatenated-markup assignment must turn the hostile-id check red, and flattening the doc/item grouping must turn the grouping check red.

tests.name: t2: one discrete element per requirement, every string via textContent, id + statement + rationale present, doc-level first then itemRef groups
t2: hostile content — an id with * _ ` [ and a statement with <script> come back character-for-character identical and create no child element
t2: malformed record table — non-array requirements, non-object entry, non-string id/statement, scope:'item' with no itemRef, and two entries sharing one FrId
t2 (contract): DOCS_FR_SOURCE contains no markup assignment (comments stripped first) and the shell's injection-site count is still exactly one
t2: the item CSS fragment references only --it-* variables
t2 (mutation): replace textContent with a concatenated assignment -> the hostile-id test fails
t2 (mutation): flatten the doc/item grouping -> the grouping test fails
